title: Check: How Mail Knows Where to Go

questions.prompt: For carol@cs.example.edu, what domain does the sender look up the MX for?
Put the sender's steps in order.
options: Query MX, strip the domain, send, DNS answers
Send, then query MX if it bounces
Strip the domain, query MX, DNS answers, send to the address of the MX host
Query the PTR, strip the domain, send

questions.prompt: A domain has MX 5 a.example.com and MX 50 b.example.com. Which does a sender try first?
options: a, because lower numbers are preferred

questions.prompt: Two MX records with the same priority share the load between them.
In PHP, which function returns a domain's mail hosts and their weights? (function name)
marshall.edu's single MX is priority 0. What does the 0 mean?
options: It's the most preferred (and only) choice

questions.prompt: A domain with no MX records but with an A record can still receive mail.

options: Send mail to the root servers
This domain accepts no mail, so bounce at once
